speaker_role: student (Yale sophomore) reviewing her own FERPA admissions file
key_insights: Application went through a first reviewer, then was reportedly routed into what the file labeled a 'diversity bin' for a second, separate review
The alumni/senior interviewer gave a numeric rating of 'average' but then wrote a much more positive narrative report, showing that a numeric score and the accompanying prose comments can diverge
Reader notes emphasized how the applicant connected multiple interests (language and politics) together, framed as evidence of coherence rather than a scattered profile
Reader notes flagged first-generation, low-income status and being local to the college's home city, plus a local community-nonprofit internship, as differentiating factors
Recommendation letters were described by a reader as 'not form letters,' which the reader read as evidence of a genuine relationship with the recommending teacher
The file explicitly recorded 'likely nomination: no,' i.e. staff assessed her as a less-likely admit at that stage, yet she was ultimately admitted
specific_numbers_or_facts: Senior alumni interviewer gave a numeric rating of 3 ('average'), per the applicant's notes
Second reviewer gave an overall rating described as 'two plus,' per the applicant's notes
notable_or_distinctive: The 'diversity bin' routing and explicit 'likely nomination: no' marking are unusually specific internal-process details not commonly seen in similar file-review videos.
reliability_notes: Same genre as prior Yale/Stanford FERPA file-review videos already in the knowledge base (different applicant, new data). Single self-reported account from handwritten notes taken during a no-device viewing session, so some terminology (e.g. 'diversity bin') may be the applicant's own inference rather than an official term; auto-captions are largely clean.
